label: 100 AD
note: Only a single largest city is reliably attested this early; full top-5 rankings need a richer dataset than currently exists here (see TODO in docs/SPEC.md).

cities.name: Rome
cities.blurb: Capital of the Roman Empire near its territorial peak; likely the first city in history to reach a million people, fed by grain shipped from Egypt. Modelski estimates a far smaller ~450,000.

label: 500 AD
note: Single largest city only (see note on 100 AD).

cities.name: Constantinople
cities.blurb: Capital of the Eastern Roman (Byzantine) Empire, ringed by the Theodosian Walls; by this point Rome itself had shrunk to a fraction of its former size. Modelski gives ~400,000.

label: 800 AD
note: Sources disagree on which city actually led: Chandler picks Baghdad, Morris and Modelski instead credit Chang'an.

cities.name: Baghdad
cities.blurb: Newly built round city of the Abbasid Caliphate under Harun al-Rashid; a center of the Islamic Golden Age's translation and scholarship movement. Morris and Modelski instead rank Chang'an, China (800,000–1,000,000) as larger this year.

label: 1000 AD
note: Wide three-way disagreement: Modelski favors Baghdad, Morris favors Kaifeng, Chandler's much lower Cordoba figure reflects a stricter estimation method.

cities.name: Baghdad
cities.blurb: Home to the House of Wisdom translation movement and one of history's great concentrations of scholarship. Morris instead credits Kaifeng, China (~1,000,000); Chandler's Cordoba estimate is only ~350,000.

label: 1200 AD
note: Morris and Modelski both point to cities near 1,000,000 (Hangzhou, Baghdad); Chandler's Hangzhou figure is far lower.

cities.name: Hangzhou
cities.blurb: Capital of the Southern Song dynasty. Marco Polo, visiting decades later, would describe it as the most magnificent city he had ever seen. Chandler's estimate is only ~255,000; Modelski instead ranks Baghdad similarly large.

label: 1300 AD
note: Single largest city only; Morris and Modelski differ by more than 3x on Hangzhou's population.

cities.name: Hangzhou
cities.blurb: Under Mongol Yuan rule, Hangzhou remained a major commercial hub; the traveler Ibn Battuta later called it the largest city he had ever seen. Modelski's estimate is only ~432,000.

label: 1500 AD
note: Single largest city only; the three sources range from 600,000 to 1,000,000.

cities.name: Beijing
cities.blurb: Ming dynasty capital, rebuilt around the Forbidden City complex completed in 1420.

label: 1700 AD
note: Strong three-way disagreement — Chandler, Morris and Modelski each name a different city (Constantinople, Beijing, Ayutthaya) as world's largest this year.

cities.name: Constantinople
cities.blurb: Ottoman capital bridging Europe and Asia, with a majority non-Muslim population of Greeks, Armenians, and Jews alongside Turks. Morris instead ranks Beijing largest; Modelski, the now-vanished Siamese capital Ayutthaya.

label: 1800 AD
note: Rare agreement — all three sources rank this city largest this year.

cities.name: Beijing
cities.blurb: Qing dynasty capital; China's economy and population were, by most estimates, still the largest in the world.

cities.name: London
cities.blurb: Capital of the British Empire at the dawn of the Victorian era — the first city in the world to industrialize at scale.

note: All three sources closely agree — confidence is much higher from this point on.

cities.name: London
cities.blurb: The world's largest city and financial capital of an empire spanning roughly a quarter of the globe's land area.

cities.name: New York
cities.blurb: Newly consolidated as a five-borough city; its Art Deco skyline was still a few years from completion.

note: From here on, cities are true top-5 rankings (UN World Urbanization Prospects, urban agglomeration). Exact figures are recalled approximations pending verification against the live UN WUP CSV — see TODO in docs/SPEC.md.

cities.name: New York
cities.blurb: Post-war economic boom capital; the newly opened UN headquarters sat on the East River.

cities.name: Tokyo
cities.blurb: Rebuilding rapidly after much of the city was destroyed by firebombing in 1945.

cities.name: London
cities.blurb: Still recovering from the Blitz; the Festival of Britain was a year away.

cities.name: Paris
cities.blurb: Post-war reconstruction underway under the Marshall Plan.

cities.name: Moscow
cities.blurb: Capital of the Soviet Union amid its early Cold War superpower buildup.

cities.name: Tokyo
cities.blurb: Ten years after hosting the 1964 Olympics, now the world's largest urban agglomeration by a wide margin.

cities.name: New York
cities.blurb: Facing a fiscal crisis that nearly bankrupted the city this same year.

cities.name: Shanghai
cities.blurb: China's largest industrial city, though still closed to most foreign visitors under Mao-era policy.

cities.name: Mexico City
cities.blurb: Among the fastest-growing cities in the world this decade, straining infrastructure and air quality.

cities.name: São Paulo
cities.blurb: Brazil's industrial engine, growing explosively during the country's 'economic miracle' years.

cities.name: Tokyo
cities.blurb: Still the world's largest urban agglomeration, a title it had held for decades.

cities.name: Mexico City
cities.blurb: One of the largest metro areas in the Americas, built partly atop the drained lakebed of Aztec Tenochtitlan.

cities.name: New York
cities.blurb: Entering the new millennium as a global financial and cultural capital.

cities.name: São Paulo
cities.blurb: South America's largest metropolis and financial center.

cities.name: Mumbai
cities.blurb: India's financial capital, its population swelling with rural-to-urban migration.

label: 2025 (est.)
note: Figures are order-of-magnitude estimates from recalled UN projections, not a fresh pull — verify before treating as current.

cities.name: Tokyo
cities.blurb: Still the world's largest urban agglomeration, despite Japan's shrinking overall population.

cities.name: Delhi
cities.blurb: On track to overtake Tokyo as the world's largest city within the next decade on most UN projections.

cities.name: Shanghai
cities.blurb: China's largest city and a global financial and shipping hub.

cities.name: Dhaka
cities.blurb: One of the fastest-growing megacities in the world, and among the most densely populated.

cities.name: São Paulo
cities.blurb: Still South America's largest metropolis a century after its coffee-boom growth spurt began.
